feed.title: Protik Roychowdhury — Ideas
feed.subtitle: Essays on AI product strategy, trust in high-stakes products, product leadership, and marketplace design.

entry.title: The meter is always running
entry.summary: What generative AI actually costs when you are the one signing for it. A product leader's guide to GenAI unit economics, model routing, and the hidden costs nobody puts in the demo.

entry.title: Marking the model's homework
entry.summary: How we evaluate LLM features before shipping. A practical playbook for AI evals: vignette-based evaluation, eval suites as release gates, harm taxonomies, tiered escalation to humans, and regression testing prompts like code.

entry.title: Everybody wants the home screen
entry.summary: What consumer growth actually looks like inside a superapp — ML-based personalisation, behavioural segmentation, onboarding funnels and engagement loops at Grab, where every vertical competes for the same home screen.

entry.title: From consumer app to $20M enterprise ARR
entry.summary: How Intellect pivoted from a consumer mental-health app to a B2B2C enterprise SaaS platform — multi-tenancy, configurable compliance, enterprise billing, and the buyer-versus-user tension, told by the VP Product who ran the platform.

entry.title: The same conversations
entry.summary: Product managers often stall not because they lack skill, but because their strengths go unchecked — helpfulness becomes overcommitment, diligence becomes output theatre, and loyalty becomes stagnation. And often the real cause is not the PM at all.

entry.title: Vibe-coding the nuptial archive
entry.summary: A product person who builds for millions of users couldn't face selecting 200 wedding photos from 2,000. So after a year of procrastinating, he vibe-coded a Tinder-style voting app in a weekend.

entry.title: Payments at scale: what I learned about fintech at Grab
entry.summary: Lessons from leading Growth, Engagement & Loyalty and Driver Rentals at Grab — building payments infrastructure, financial services, and engagement loops for millions of users across Southeast Asia.

entry.title: Marketplace lessons from Ola: supply-demand, fraud, and driver economics
entry.summary: Product lessons from building marketplace products at Ola — supply-demand optimisation, dynamic pricing, fraud prevention, and two-sided marketplace design at India's largest ride-hailing platform.

entry.title: The anatomy of startup blind spots
entry.summary: Three startups, three different mistakes, one common thread. Lessons from building Bhalu.com, Croak.it, and Athlete Diaries — on pivoting, persistence, and co-founder alignment.

entry.title: The architecture of algorithmic trust
entry.summary: Trust in AI products has three layers: transparency, control, and recourse. A cross-domain framework from marketplace fraud prevention, clinical AI safety, and payments integrity.

entry.title: The architecture of consequential AI
entry.summary: What's different about shipping AI when you have regulators, clinical governance, and real harm potential. Lessons from building GenAI features in mental health at Intellect.

entry.title: What product leaders actually do
entry.summary: The job of a senior product leader isn't roadmaps and sprints. It's judgment under uncertainty, saying no to good ideas, and building systems so others can exercise judgment too.

entry.title: The great unbundling of product management: why 2026 belongs to the impact architect
entry.summary: AI is absorbing the mechanical parts of product work. The PMs who thrive in 2026 are Impact Architects — people who frame problems, make resource bets, and build conviction in teams.

entry.title: The ROI of care: investing in mental health as infrastructure for performance
entry.summary: Mental health isn't a perk. It's infrastructure. And like all infrastructure, its value isn't captured in a single metric — it's felt in everything that sits on top of it.

entry.title: What humans still do best, and why that should shape the future of AI in mental health
entry.summary: AI will transform mental health care. But not by replacing humans. By doing what humans can't — so humans can do what AI can't.

entry.title: Designing for trust in mental health apps: why UX is care
entry.summary: In mental health products, trust isn't a feature — it's the product. Five UX principles for building experiences that earn trust in high-stakes, vulnerable contexts.

entry.title: When AI becomes an echo chamber: the ethical risk to mental health
entry.summary: AI chatbots that only validate without challenging create a therapeutic echo chamber. What the mental health industry needs to do to build AI tools that actually help people get better.

entry.title: How AI is personalising mental health support at scale
entry.summary: AI is changing the personalisation equation in mental health care. Here's how — and what it means for product leaders building in this space.
